name: Step-by-Step Garage Remodel Timeline: From Planning to Final Inspection

step.name: Step 1: Define your layout and confirm project requirements
step.text: Determine exactly how you plan to use the space, whether for organized vehicle storage, a dedicated workshop, or clean utility space. Take basic measurements, outline where cabinets, workbenches, and power tools will sit, and check with your local building department to determine what building, electrical, or mechanical permits your scope will require before ordering materials.

step.name: Step 2: Inspect structural components and existing utilities
step.text: Examine the concrete slab for major cracks, water intrusion, or settling issues that need repair. Check the roof framing, exterior walls, and garage doors for wear or rot. A licensed contractor evaluates the current electrical service panel to confirm it can handle added lighting, dedicated outlets, or heating equipment without overloading your home.

step.name: Step 3: Secure building permits and order construction materials
step.text: Submit your plans to the local building department to get all required permits issued. Construction should never start before permits are in hand, as unpermitted work risks stop-work notices and costly teardowns. Once approvals are confirmed, order your framing timber, drywall, insulation, and finish components so work can proceed smoothly.

step.name: Step 4: Complete rough framing, electrical, and insulation work
step.text: Tackle any necessary structural repairs, custom wall framing, and rough-in work for electrical wiring, dedicated circuits, and plumbing lines. Once rough inspections are passed, install code-compliant wall and ceiling insulation to control temperature swings and prepare the envelope for interior finishes.

step.name: Step 5: Hang drywall, apply finishes, and schedule final inspections
step.text: Hang and tape drywall, apply texture, and paint the walls with durable interior coatings. Complete finish carpentry, trim, and specialty flooring, then coordinate final municipal inspections to ensure all structural, mechanical, and electrical work complies with local standards.
